title: resolveFinalPath infinite-loops on a recorded rename cycle (mv a b; mv b a)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-203 finding (2026-07-25): while building the layered lineage walk, resolveFinalPath (src/reconstruction_lineage.ts) was found to follow the rename chain without a seen-set, so a transcript that records `mv a b` followed by `mv b a` — which real sessions do produce when a rename is undone — makes it loop forever rather than terminating on the cycle. The new layered walk in jfred/src/layered_lineage.ts avoids this by carrying a shared seen-set across both directions, and the engine's version was deliberately left untouched so the fix could be scoped and verified on its own. Add a seen-set (or an explicit cycle error) to resolveFinalPath and every other rename-chain walker that shares the pattern, with a unit test that records the two-hop cycle and asserts termination. No live scenario is known to trigger it yet, so a synthetic fixture is acceptable evidence.

title: renderRevisionText unconditionally appends a trailing newline, so files without one can never blob-match
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-187 finding (2026-07-25): renderRevisionText renders a revision as linesTextOf(rev).join("\n") + "\n" — the trailing newline is unconditional. A file whose real bytes do NOT end in a newline therefore can never hash-match its recorded blob. In the 68-file M sweep this produced a 2/2 correlation: exactly 2 of the 68 baseline blobs lack a trailing newline (docs/design/architecture.md ending 0x2e, docs/design/milestones.md ending 0x2e) and those are exactly the 2 baselineBlobMatched=false rows. The same artifact also corrupts the diskMatched comparison for 3 further files. Fixing this means the engine must carry a 'final line had no newline' bit, which touches the LineEntry vocabulary and every producer/consumer of it — CONFIRM the design with the user before implementing (open question 2 in plans/implementation-notes-tasks-223-224-184-203-207-187.md). Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 187 — the M-file sweep (68 files)".

title: Extend the task-224 seed clamp to the two sibling backup stampers (needs a reproducer first)
description: DEFER UNTIL AFTER THE LAYER 1 VIEW MILESTONE (spec S18, tasks #230-#239) IS COMPLETE. Task-224 follow-up (2026-07-25): task 224 fixed the non-monotonic ladder by giving backup-sourced seeds a two-sided placement window via clampSeedBetweenPreviousAndEdit (jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar.ts), but wired it into ONE proven site — seedStaleEditBases in jfred/src/reconstruction_reseed.ts. Two sibling stampers apply the identical `timestamp: <backupTime>` pattern and therefore share the defect CLASS: backupAfterWriteFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:90-96, used by reversedEditBaseSeed at reconstruction_reseed.ts:157) and backupWritesFor (reconstruction_sidecar.ts:116-122, used at reconstruction_beacons.ts:158 and via latestBackupWriteFor at reconstruction_beacons.ts:56). title: Layer 1 Detail View: show image files as images, with zoom controls in the drawer header
description:
User feedback 2026-07-27, after task 294 shipped syntax highlighting: clicking a .png bubble showed the file's decoded bytes. An immediate fix landed WITH 294 — jfred/webapp/layer1-file-view.ts now sniffs the first 1024 characters for a NUL or a high share of U+FFFD replacement characters and renders the sentence "Binary file — not shown as text." instead of thousands of rows of mojibake (see `looksBinary`). THIS task replaces that placeholder for IMAGES specifically.

Requirement: clicking a node for an image file (png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, svg, bmp, ico) shows the IMAGE in the Detail View drawer, zoomed to fit the drawer on first render, with zoom in / zoom out / reset buttons in the drawer's HEADER — the same row that will later carry the 'side-by-side diff | inline diff | show full content' controls the current webapp's Detail Revision pane already has. Put them where those will go rather than inventing a second control strip.

The bytes must reach the browser as an image. GET /api/layer1-file currently reads with utf8 and returns { content: string }, which destroys binary data, so it needs a binary path (base64, or a raw byte response with the right content-type) — chosen for BOTH the on-disk case and the git-show case, since a commit node reads the blob out of the repository rather than the working tree. Non-image binaries keep the placeholder sentence.

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-file-view.ts (looksBinary + renderFileContentInto), jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts (openNodeDrawer and the header it fills), jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_file.ts (the route), jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css (.drawer .dhead, .dbody).

title: Layer 1 View: an expanded ruler row's file list overprints the ruler rows below it
description:
User bug report with screenshot, 2026-07-27. Repro: load the Layer 1 View on a real project and click a ruler row shared by several nodes so it expands into its file list (task 284's `.tickfiles`). If the list is long it is drawn straight over the ruler rows beneath it — in the reported screenshot `07-16 21:24:28.15 (28)` is buried under `reconstruction_graph.ts on disk`, and the rows below keep their original y positions.

User's hypothesis, confirmed correct: the y coordinate of every ruler row below the clicked one is not recomputed when the list opens, so nothing accounts for the list's height.

The signed-off design already exists in plans/layer1-mockup.html lines 700-711 and 836-848: `resolveOffsets` takes an `extraAt` map keyed by the LAST instant the expanded row absorbed, carrying the list's height in AXIS pixels (screen px divided by the zoom, because the gutter sits outside the zoom), and the layout runs TWICE — a draft pass to learn which instants the printed row absorbed and how many files those hold, then the real pass with `extraAt` fed in. The mockup deliberately REJECTS drawing the list as an overlay over the canvas: feeding the height into the layout is what makes a bubble spanning the expanded instant GROW instead of being written over.

Implementing it means giving `layOutNodeLadders` in jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts an equivalent extra-height input, and having the expansion in jfred/webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts trigger a full re-layout and re-render rather than only injecting the list into the tick. NOTE: that axis module is shared with the server (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts imports layOutNodeLadders), so the server's own call must keep today's behaviour and every existing placement test must still pass.

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-tick-files.ts, jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts (renderRulerTicks / renderLayer1Stage), jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts (relayOutLayer1View), jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts. This is task-284 code and predates the 292/294-297 batch.

title: Decide how duplicate snapshots resolve when multiple File History Snapshot folders are configured
description:
User question 2026-07-27 while testing task 296: "How are duplicates (hash and @vN) handled when using multiple FHS paths?"

VERIFIED CURRENT ANSWER: they are NOT handled, because nothing consumes the list yet. Task 296 shipped the picker that stores multiple file-history folders and task 297 saves them to ~/.jfred-layer1-settings.json and .config/debugConfig.json, but the Layer 1 View reads NO file-history at all (spec S18 — it compares a working tree against a git tree, which is the whole point of the task-238 acceptance test). The list is stored and carried for the layer that will read it: layer 3's file-history snapshot beacons (jfred/src/layered_snapshot_beacons.ts, task 201).

The collision is real and must be decided BEFORE that layer reads more than one folder. A file-history store is <root>/<sessionId>/<blob>, where a blob name looks like `971e94bac3cb2811@v2` — so two configured roots can hold the SAME sessionId and the SAME <hash>@vN with DIFFERENT bytes. The obvious case is one root being a backup or partial copy of the other, which is exactly the ~/Programming/jot-recovery/claude-data/file-history vs ~/.claude/file-history pair this project already works with.

Questions to settle with the user:
1. first-root-wins, last-root-wins, or refuse and report a conflict into the health sink the way task 176 made cross-source contradictions do?
2. is identical-bytes-in-both a silent no-op, or still worth reporting?
3. does the ORDER of the folders in the picker define precedence? If so the list's order is load-bearing and the UI should say so.

Relevant files: jfred/src/reconstruction_sidecar_reader.ts (the single-root reader and its ~/.claude/file-history default chain), jfred/src/layered_snapshot_beacons.ts, jfred/src/reconstruction_multi_source_join.ts (the existing precedent for merging several sources), jfred/webapp/layer1-source-paths.ts (where the list lives client-side).

title: Layer 1 View: a Cancel button while a project is loading
description:
User request 2026-07-27. A Layer 1 build takes ~10 s on a real project and there is currently no way to stop one — picking the wrong folder means waiting it out. Add a Cancel button that is shown ONLY while the loading progress bar is up, and hidden the moment the load finishes, fails, or is cancelled.

Cancelling must actually abort the in-flight request rather than only hiding the bar: GET /api/layer1-view is read as an NDJSON progress stream (jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts `readLayer1ViewStream`), so the fetch needs an AbortController the button can trigger, and the reader loop has to treat an abort as a clean stop rather than an error in the crumb. Decide what the stage shows afterwards — the S18 precedent is that loadLayer1View already clears the crumb, the stage and the File Nav before a build starts, so a cancelled load leaves an empty stage and the crumb should say so plainly.

There is prior art for the control in the classic webapp: task 164 added a Cancel-with-confirm on the pane-scoped progress overlay. Reuse its wording and its confirm behaviour rather than inventing a second idiom, but note the Layer 1 page deliberately does not import from webapp/views/ (see the header of jfred/webapp/layer1-file-view.ts for why).

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts (showLayer1Progress / hideLayer1Progress / readLayer1ViewStream), jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts (loadLayer1View), jfred/webapp/layer1.html (the .loadbar block), jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css.

title: Layer 1 View: show a progress bar during 'resolving the ruler', which currently reports nothing
description:
User report 2026-07-27, refined: the loadbar must show progress while the 'resolving the ruler' stage is on screen. Today the bar goes quiet once 'reading file history' completes, and the page reads as frozen for the rest of the build — the same complaint task 149 fixed for the classic viewer's phase 4.

The route announces its stages from jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts, which EXPORTS the labels so tests assert the same strings the route emits: LAYER1_PROGRESS_LABEL_WALKING_FOLDER, _READING_TREE, _READING_HISTORY, _PLACING_REPO_ONLY and _RESOLVING_RULER. The last of those is the one the user watched sit still. `resolving the ruler` is layOutNodeLadders (jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts) over every pair ladder plus one single-node ladder per orphan — on a ~900-pair repo that is ~900+ ladders resolved in one synchronous pass that emits no progress at all, so the label appears and nothing moves until the whole build finishes.

Deliverable: 'resolving the ruler' reports incrementing progress while it runs — a COUNTER, not a static label, because task 163 established that an incrementing count is what stops a long stage reading as a hang. Feed the ProgressSink from inside the ladder loop, and check the neighbouring stages the same way while you are there: the per-pair commit-history walk (jfred/src/layer1_commit_history.ts runs one `git log` per paired file) is the other obvious silent stretch.

Relevant files: jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1.ts (the stage labels and the ProgressSink calls), jfred/webapp/layer1-ruler-axis.ts (layOutNodeLadders — NOTE it is shared with the client-side re-layout in jfred/webapp/layer1-filter.ts, which must not gain a server-only progress dependency), jfred/src/layer1_commit_history.ts, jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts (the NDJSON stream), jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts (the client-side bar). Related but separate: task 302 adds a Cancel button to the same bar.

title: Layer 1 View: the JSONL Nav must show a progress indicator while it builds its list
description:
User report 2026-07-27. Symptom: after the timeline is displayed and the ruler resolved, the JSONLs pane shows the empty-state message "no JSONLs touched this project's files" and then a few seconds later populates with the real list. That message is a LIE during the load — it states a finished result while the work is still running — and it reads as the pane being broken or the project having no transcripts.

Cause: renderLayer1View draws the stage first and then fires loadLayer1Sessions() WITHOUT awaiting it, deliberately, so the session scan does not delay the timeline (jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts). GET /api/layer1-sessions parses every JSONL under the configured source folders — measured at ~4 s over 629 transcripts on the user's real config — and until it answers, jfred/webapp/layer1-sessions.ts holds an empty `sessions` array, so renderSessionPane falls straight to its empty-state row.

Deliverable: while the session list is being fetched and filtered the pane shows a progress indicator, and the empty-state message appears ONLY once the fetch has completed and genuinely produced nothing. Reuse the existing loadbar idiom rather than inventing a second one (jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts owns .loadbar / .loadbar-fill / .loadbar-label, styled in layer1-styles.css). The pane is narrow, so either a slim bar or a labelled 'scanning N JSONL folders…' row is acceptable — pick one and say why in the code.

Consider whether the endpoint should stream NDJSON progress the way /api/layer1-view already does (jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_route.ts is the server precedent, readLayer1ViewStream in jfred/webapp/layer1-progress.ts the client half): a per-file count turns a 4 s blank into a visibly advancing scan. If that is too much, a plain indeterminate indicator still fixes the reported confusion.

This is the first task filed under the user's standing rule (2026-07-27): anything that takes a while to load shows a progress bar.

Relevant files: jfred/webapp/layer1-sessions.ts (loadLayer1Sessions, renderSessionPane and its .navempty row), jfred/webapp/layer1-page.ts (renderLayer1View), jfred/src/viewer_api_layer1_sessions.ts (the endpoint), jfred/webapp/layer1-styles.css. Related: task 302 (cancel button on the main loadbar) and task 303 (progress during 'resolving the ruler').

title: Layer 1 View: select two nodes on a bubble's lane to diff those two revisions in the Detail View
description:
User request 2026-07-27 (feature). Select two nodes on one file bubble's timeline and the Detail View shows a diff of those two revisions of the file. Detail View header buttons: [diff side-by-side / diff inline] [full content] [export as patch].

Today clicking ONE node opens the drawer on that node's bytes at that instant (task 257, jfred/webapp/layer1-drawer.ts). This adds a two-node selection within the SAME bubble's lane — commit-to-commit, commit-to-on-disk, or on-disk-to-commit — and shows the diff between them instead of one file's contents.

Open questions for whoever implements:
- How the second node is picked. Shift-click is the selection idiom the File Nav folders and the JSONLs pane already use, so it is the obvious candidate.
- How the pair is shown on the lane. A single clicked node already gets highlightLandedElement's marks, and two selected nodes must read as a PAIR with a direction (older = base, newer = target).
- A selection spanning two DIFFERENT bubbles is out of scope: refuse it visibly rather than silently diffing unrelated files.

The three header buttons go in the drawer's header row — the same place task 299 puts the image zoom controls. Do not add a second control strip.

REUSE rather than reimplement. The classic webapp already has the whole diff surface: jfred/webapp/views/details-diff.ts renders side-by-side and inline (renderDiffVsBase / renderRevisionDiff); the server has GET /api/diff (handleDiffRequest in jfred/src/viewer_server_routes.ts, jfred/src/viewer_api_diffs.ts) and GET /api/range-patch (handleRangePatchRequest, jfred/src/render_git_diff.ts), which is what 'export as patch' wants.

BUT note the constraint that shaped this drawer: the Layer 1 page deliberately imports NOTHING from webapp/views/, because that drags app-routes.ts → inspector.ts → timeline-*.ts — the entire classic app — into a page that loads only layer1-*.js (see the header comment of jfred/webapp/layer1-file-view.ts).
